notes: Nineteenth-Century Spanish America : A Cultural History provides a panoramic and accessible introduction to the era in which Latin America took its first steps into the Modern Age. Including colorful characters like circus clowns, prostitutes, bullfighters, street puppeteers, and bestselling authors, this book maps vivid and often surprising combinations of the new and the old, the high and the low, and the political and the cultural. Christopher Conway shows that beneath the diversity of the New World there was a deeper structure of shared patterns of cultural creation and meaning. Whether it be the ways that people of refinement from different countries used the same rules of etiquette, or how commoners shared their stories through the same types of songs, Conway creates a multidisciplinary framework for understanding the culture of an entire hemisphere. The book opens with key themes that will help students and scholars understand the century, such as the civilization and barbarism binary, urbanism, the divide between conservatives and liberals, and transculturation. In the chapters that follow, Conway weaves transnational trends together with brief case studies and compelling snapshots that help us understand the period. How much did books and photographs cost in the nineteenth century? What was the dominant style in painting? What kinds of ballroom dancing were popular? Richly illustrated with striking photographs and lithographs, this is a book that invites the reader to rediscover a past age that is not quite past, still resonating into the present."

item.annotation: Detailed and well-documented account of Peruvian military doctrine during crucial two decades preceding reformist military regime of 1968-80. Nationalist reformist thought among Peru's officers evolved out of adoption of French and German doctrines of total war, strengthened by counter-insurgency concepts pushed by US military during late 1950s and early 1960s. Author stresses importance of shifting position of Peruvian military in nation's politics. Already 1962 coup heralded break of majority of senior officer corps with representatives of export-oriented oligarchy. When "neo-populist" option (Belaúnde Terry) failed to realize their nationalist and integrationist goals, most officers were ready to establish institutionalized military regime of 1968. Conventional interpretation, following that of V. Villanueva and others, couched in Marxist terminology.

notes: Nineteenth-Century Spanish America : A Cultural History provides a panoramic and accessible introduction to the era in which Latin America took its first steps into the Modern Age. Including colorful characters like circus clowns, prostitutes, bullfighters, street puppeteers, and bestselling authors, this book maps vivid and often surprising combinations of the new and the old, the high and the low, and the political and the cultural. Christopher Conway shows that beneath the diversity of the New World there was a deeper structure of shared patterns of cultural creation and meaning. Whether it be the ways that people of refinement from different countries used the same rules of etiquette, or how commoners shared their stories through the same types of songs, Conway creates a multidisciplinary framework for understanding the culture of an entire hemisphere. The book opens with key themes that will help students and scholars understand the century, such as the civilization and barbarism binary, urbanism, the divide between conservatives and liberals, and transculturation. In the chapters that follow, Conway weaves transnational trends together with brief case studies and compelling snapshots that help us understand the period. How much did books and photographs cost in the nineteenth century? What was the dominant style in painting? What kinds of ballroom dancing were popular? Richly illustrated with striking photographs and lithographs, this is a book that invites the reader to rediscover a past age that is not quite past, still resonating into the present."

item.annotation: Detailed and well-documented account of Peruvian military doctrine during crucial two decades preceding reformist military regime of 1968-80. Nationalist reformist thought among Peru's officers evolved out of adoption of French and German doctrines of total war, strengthened by counter-insurgency concepts pushed by US military during late 1950s and early 1960s. Author stresses importance of shifting position of Peruvian military in nation's politics. Already 1962 coup heralded break of majority of senior officer corps with representatives of export-oriented oligarchy. When "neo-populist" option (Belaúnde Terry) failed to realize their nationalist and integrationist goals, most officers were ready to establish institutionalized military regime of 1968. Conventional interpretation, following that of V. Villanueva and others, couched in Marxist terminology.

notes: Nineteenth-Century Spanish America : A Cultural History provides a panoramic and accessible introduction to the era in which Latin America took its first steps into the Modern Age. Including colorful characters like circus clowns, prostitutes, bullfighters, street puppeteers, and bestselling authors, this book maps vivid and often surprising combinations of the new and the old, the high and the low, and the political and the cultural. Christopher Conway shows that beneath the diversity of the New World there was a deeper structure of shared patterns of cultural creation and meaning. Whether it be the ways that people of refinement from different countries used the same rules of etiquette, or how commoners shared their stories through the same types of songs, Conway creates a multidisciplinary framework for understanding the culture of an entire hemisphere. The book opens with key themes that will help students and scholars understand the century, such as the civilization and barbarism binary, urbanism, the divide between conservatives and liberals, and transculturation. In the chapters that follow, Conway weaves transnational trends together with brief case studies and compelling snapshots that help us understand the period. How much did books and photographs cost in the nineteenth century? What was the dominant style in painting? What kinds of ballroom dancing were popular? Richly illustrated with striking photographs and lithographs, this is a book that invites the reader to rediscover a past age that is not quite past, still resonating into the present."

item.annotation: Detailed and well-documented account of Peruvian military doctrine during crucial two decades preceding reformist military regime of 1968-80. Nationalist reformist thought among Peru's officers evolved out of adoption of French and German doctrines of total war, strengthened by counter-insurgency concepts pushed by US military during late 1950s and early 1960s. Author stresses importance of shifting position of Peruvian military in nation's politics. Already 1962 coup heralded break of majority of senior officer corps with representatives of export-oriented oligarchy. When "neo-populist" option (Belaúnde Terry) failed to realize their nationalist and integrationist goals, most officers were ready to establish institutionalized military regime of 1968. Conventional interpretation, following that of V. Villanueva and others, couched in Marxist terminology.
